prose: Retired with its instrument, no_daemon_required.sh, under ST0097; nothing runs it now.
note:
N/A, its criterion AC-07.5 withdrawn: AC-07.5 was MET while its instrument lived, and its instrument, no_daemon_required.sh, drove a dehydrated estate through the CLI by way of intent/.intentfiles, which the 3.5.0 canon format folded into each record's realised flag (0ab6485e4). No Rust test proves the dehydrated-estate claim itself (routing_is_opt_in.rs's with_no_daemon_the_answers_are_the_same proves the servable verbs answer with no daemon, which is narrower). Retired under ST0097 on hv decision 88, 2026-11-23, relayed by vc.

The note before retirement: STATE UNCHANGED, CAVEAT RECORDED 2026-08-31 (vc), from a sweep of every green row citing a MANUAL instrument. Re-driven, the tool exits 2: arm B (structural -- intent-cli declares no intentd dependency, no socket client in sources) PASSES, and arm A (behavioural -- a dehydrated estate answers every read) REFUSES with 'an intentd process is already running, this arm cannot distinguish a daemon-free read from a daemon-served one while it is up'. THAT IS A REFUSAL AND NOT A FAILURE, which is why the row stays green rather than going red -- red asserts the cited artefact fails, and it does not. WHAT IS TRUE AND WAS NOT RECORDED: the behavioural half is NOT RE-VERIFIABLE ON THIS MACHINE while a daemon runs, and one runs essentially always with four sessions live. So the green rests on a moment nobody can reproduce on demand. Same shape as this estate's declared exclusions for shutdown and launchd: confirming the property costs the thing every peer depends on. Re-establishing it needs a scheduled daemon-down window, which is hv's to authorise, not a node's to take.
